PSHE & RSE and Citizenship
PSHE (Personal, Social, Health Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) form a core part of our Personal Development program at Eton Dorney school and is delivered through regular, planned, and timetabled lessons. Working closely with parents, our curriculum and learning schedule is also adapted whenever required to meet the needs of our own pupils.
Our lessons provide a platform for our pupils of all ages to develop values, knowledge, skills, and attributes needed for their holistic development now, for their next steps, and in their future. The knowledge, skills and attributes acquired help students form and maintain healthy relationships, stay healthy, safe, and prepare them for life, whether education, employment, or training.
The delivery of PSHE & RSE is student centered and promotes personal pupil progress through exploring their existing knowledge, understanding, and beliefs. Pupil progress is also achieved by clarifying misconceptions, building on existing knowledge and skills, and developing awareness of a wider range of attitudes and values.
Our school follows the PSHE Association program, with learning complimented by a variety of resources from Jigsaw PSHE, BBC Teach RSE, NSPCC learning, School Wellbeing, TES, NHS resources, TALKABOUT, and other resources relevant to our pupils needs and the existing cohort.
Citizenship is taught using a variety of programs and resources including ASDAN qualifications, Votes for Schools, and PSHE association resources.

Careers & Work Related Learning
Eton Dorney Therapeutic School is committed to providing a high-quality careers education, information, advice, and guidance (CEIAG) programme to all students and their parents. In line with the statutory guidance produced by the DFE and the Gatsby Benchmarks, students receive careers advice embedded into the curriculum in addition to dedicated one-to-one opportunities and group work.
CEIAG is incorporated into all-year groups through careers workshops from a variety of professional and trades persons to stimulate the interests of students and to inspire them to reach their full potential. Parents, local organisations, and friends of Eton Dorney support our careers programme through presentations and workshops with students, as well as opportunities for our students to engage in work experience placements.
All staff acknowledge an obligation to provide effective and measurable careers education and advice to all students. We recognise that all students have the right to expect that the school will help them to make informed decisions about the opportunities open to them when they leave Eton Dorney.
The Careers Education within the curriculum is interconnected with the Personal Development Programmes and the bespoke transition support that our students receive.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Eton Dorney Independent Therapeutic School
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Eton Dorney Independent Therapeutic School—a specialist provision for pupils in Years 4 to 11 (ages 8–16) who may experience Social, Emotional and Mental Health Difficulties and/or have a diagnosis of Autism or associated conditions.
At Eton Dorney, we believe that education is a journey, not a destination. Every child is unique, and we are proud to offer a nurturing, inclusive environment where pupils are warmly received, understood, and encouraged to aim high. Our mission is to help each young person fulfil their potential—not just academically, but in life skills, resilience, kindness, and self-belief.
Many of the pupils who attend Eton Dorney have not found success in their education elsewhere. Here, they rebuild trust, rediscover their desire to learn, and begin to thrive. From often lower-than-expected starting points, our pupils achieve exceptionally well academically. By the time they leave us at the end of Year 11, they hold relevant qualifications that support their next steps—whether in further education, training, or employment.
Staff at Eton Dorney are confident and skilled in building positive relationships that help to break down barriers, build self-esteem, and challenge disaffection. Our teachers and support staff are highly trained to meet the needs of individual pupils, ensuring that every child receives the personalised support they need to flourish.
I feel incredibly privileged to lead this exceptional school. Our dedicated team is committed to creating a safe, creative, and inspiring learning environment where pupils flourish both within and beyond the classroom. We work closely with families, local authorities, and professionals to ensure that every child’s strengths and interests are recognised and celebrated. Together, we build a community rooted in trust, respect, compassion, and integrity.
We understand that sustained success is only possible when wellbeing is placed at the heart of the learning process. That’s why we prioritise the emotional and mental health of our pupils and staff, fostering a culture where everyone feels safe, valued, and empowered.
Places at Eton Dorney are commissioned by several local authorities, including Slough, West Berkshire, the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead, Buckinghamshire, and Reading. All pupils referred to our school have an Education, Health and Care Plan, and we take pride in tailoring our approach to meet each child’s individual needs.
Whether you are a parent seeking a high-performing, compassionate school for your child, a professional looking to join a rewarding and dynamic team, or a young person curious about what we offer—we invite you to explore Eton Dorney. This website offers just a glimpse into our vibrant school life, and we warmly welcome visits from anyone who wishes to learn more.
Together, we can make a lasting difference.
Tom Boardman Headteacher

Attendance & Absence from School
Regular attendance is important if pupils are to benefit from the full range of educational opportunities on offer at EDTS . It is very important that pupils get into, and maintain, a pattern and routine of attendance in order to support learning and good behaviour. Consistent management of pupils is supported by regular attendance. Pupils should only be kept away from school for genuine reasons. If pupils are kept off, or have appointments coming up, parents/carers are to inform the school. The school, as a matter of routine, asks for all absences.
Parents/carers are requested to telephone the school on the first day of a pupil's absence. To report your child's absence, please ring the main office by 09.00AM stating clearly their name, their class and a specific reason for their absence i.e. if they are ill please state the specific illness.
Parents/carers are requested to take annual holidays during school holidays. Requests for holidays during term-time will be declined. Where parents decide to take holidays regardless, the appropriate form must be completed. The school will record all such occasions as unauthorised absence and the local authority welfare calls may also become involved.
As a school, we aim that students' attendance is at least 95% across the year. To put this in concrete terms, the following table shows the number of school days per year missed at different percentages of attendance.
Multiply this by 5 to reflect the 5 years of secondary education and students with 95% attendance or lower across their time at the school will have missed at least 45 days (225 hours) of learning time!
We would therefore ask that you try to ensure that your son/daughter achieves the best possible attendance this year. The Winter and Spring Terms are traditionally period of seasonal illness and, whilst we want to stress that students should not attend school if they are genuinely unfit for learning, we would ask that this is kept to the minimum required for them to recover.

Curriculum Maps
At Eton Dorney Independent Therapeutic School, we believe that transparency and collaboration with families are key to supporting every child’s educational journey. To help you stay informed and engaged with your child’s learning, we are pleased to share our termly curriculum maps.
These maps provide a clear overview of what your child will be learning across each subject area, including core academic content, personal development, and therapeutic support. Whether your child is in Primary, Key Stage 3, or Key Stage 4, the curriculum is thoughtfully designed to be engaging, inclusive, and tailored to meet individual needs.
Each map outlines the topics, skills, and enrichment activities planned for the term, giving you insight into how we nurture academic progress alongside emotional wellbeing. We hope these documents will help you feel more connected to your child’s learning and better equipped to support them at home.

Art Therapy
Art therapy uses art as the primary mode of expression, alongside talking with an art therapist. It aims to reduce distress and improve social, emotional, and mental health by promoting insight, self-compassion and a sense of agency and self-worth.
During art therapy, pupils are supported by an art therapist to use art to express and articulate often complex thoughts and feelings through art making. This may be following difficult or traumatic experiences which may be hard to talk about.

Personal Development
Personal Development
Personal development is a key part of student learning at Eton Dorney School with SMSC at the heart of our school development. Our aim is for our students to leave as well-rounded and contributing members of society. Through our curriculum and other creative opportunities, our students access different experiences which develop their character, confidence, resilience, self-esteem, self-worth, life skills, and independence.
Our students leave for further education or the world of work with the necessary skills, qualities, aims in life, and the ability to set goals to realise and maximise their potential.
Our Personal development is accessed through aspects of our robust curriculum, and our trauma informed therapeutic approaches through the areas below.
• Personal, Social, Health, and Citizenship Education
• Relationships and Sex Education
• Humanities curriculum and enrichment activities
• Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural development learning
• Life skills, Work related learning, Work experience, and Careers workshops.
• Pastoral and Mental Health and Wellbeing support
• Assemblies and rewards
• Celebration of the Fundamental British Values
• Celebration of our school ethos and positive personal qualities and achievements
• Celebration of the diverse backgrounds of members of our school community

Pupil Premium
What is the pupil premium?
Introduced in 2011, the pupil premium is a sum of money given to schools each year by the Government to improve the attainment of disadvantaged children.
This is based on research showing that children from low income families perform less well at school than their peers. Often, children who are entitled to pupil premium face challenges such as poor language and communication skills, lack of confidence and issues with attendance and punctuality. The pupil premium is intended to directly benefit the children who are eligible, helping to narrow the gap between them and their classmates.

How Pupil Premium funding may be spent
Schools can choose how to spend their pupil premium money, as they are best placed to identify what would be of most benefit to the children who are eligible.

Providing extra tuition for able children.
Funding educational trips and visits.

Admissions
Admissions and Referrals
The purpose of the school’s assessment process is to determine and clarify the needs of the individual student with a view to evaluating whether these can be met by Eton Dorney Therapeutic School’s educational approach and environment.
Eton Dorney Independent Therapeutic School is a day special school for boys and girls aged 8- 18 years, however, the school currently educates students up to year 11.
We are a special school which caters for the needs of pupils who have social, emotional and mental health difficulties, including associated challenging behaviours. Many of the pupils attending the school have additional special educational needs such as autistic spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit and hyperactive disorders (ADHD) which may affect their speech and language development. All of our children will have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP)
Places for pupils are commissioned at the school by several local authorities, including Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead, Surrey, Oxfordshire, Hampshire, West Berkshire, Wokingham, Buckinghamshire and Slough.
